questions.a: The whole variety of life - species, their genes and the ecosystems they form - in a region.
Every species supports others; losing one destabilises ecosystems and removes future resources.

questions.q: Name a biodiversity-rich region of India.
questions.a: The Western Ghats (also the Himalaya and the North-East).
To arrange millions of species into groups based on similarities, making study and identification easier.

questions.q: On what basis are living things grouped?
questions.a: Body design, cell type, number of cells, mode of nutrition and evolutionary links.

questions.q: What is the basis of the two-kingdom vs five-kingdom classification?
questions.a: The five-kingdom system adds Monera, Protista and Fungi by separating prokaryotes and distinct nutrition patterns.

concepts.title: Hierarchy of Classification: Kingdom to Species

questions.q: List the hierarchy of classification from kingdom to species.
questions.a: Kingdom, phylum/division, class, order, family, genus, species.
The basic unit - organisms so similar that they can breed naturally and produce fertile young.

questions.q: Give the scientific name format of any organism.
questions.a: Two Latin words - genus first (capitalised), species second (small), written in italics, e.g. Mangifera indica.
